title: White Line: A Typed Ledger for the Edge of the Claim
description: A typed ledger for absence: epistemic gaps, ethical restraint, and contemplative negative space. It records what is missing, withheld, or unresolved under a total caution order, decays stale namings past their review horizons, and refuses to infer why anything is absent. Withholding is recorded as a boundary, never mined as missing evidence. Subtitle: Keeping missing evidence, ethical boundaries, and open questions from becoming unsupported claims Code is MIT licensed; prose and figures are CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE in the repository.

methods.name: Pure-data Python package: 11-record registry + assess_absence evaluator
methods.description: The instrument is a small Python package holding a versioned registry of eleven absence records and a staged evaluator, presented as a tested prototype.
methods.evidence: The executable instrument is a small, pure-data Python package: a versioned registry of eleven absence records and a staged evaluator, assess_absence.

methods.name: Typology of three absence kinds and four ledger states
methods.description: Records are typed EPISTEMIC, ETHICAL or CONTEMPLATIVE, and observations assign NAMED, UNRESOLVED, WITHHELD or ledger-reserved NOT_RECORDED.
methods.evidence: Each record carries one of three kinds — EPISTEMIC, ETHICAL, or CONTEMPLATIVE — and a dated observation assigns it one of four states: NAMED, UNRESOLVED, WITHHELD, or NOT_RECORDED.

methods.name: Staged intake/matching/scoring with caution order and staleness decay
methods.description: Intake screens inputs with typed events, conflicting observers resolve to the more cautious state, and dated NAMED entries decay past their review horizon.
methods.evidence: Intake normalizes and screens the input, matching keeps at most one contract-passing observation per record, and scoring assigns each record its state.

methods.name: Formal definitions/propositions each bound to a named test
methods.description: The evaluator is restated as definitions and propositions, and a table maps each to the test that exercises it, checked by tests/test_formalism.py.
methods.evidence: Every definition and proposition above names the test that exercises it, keyed by the block’s own label, and tests/test_formalism.py asserts that each row names a test that exists

methods.name: Planted-defect battery for six structural invariants
methods.description: For each of six registry invariants, a registry carrying exactly that defect is constructed to show the check rejects it while passing the real registry.
methods.evidence: Each invariant 𝑃𝑖 is accompanied by a planted-defect registry: a registry carrying exactly the defect 𝑃𝑖 guards against is constructed, and 𝑃𝑖 fails on it while passing on the real registry 𝑅.

key_findings: Under the stated contract, no input can make an absence appear more settled than its most cautious observer reported (caution monotonicity).
In a worked seven-input example with careless and adversarial inputs, intake logged five typed events and the tally was NAMED 0, UNRESOLVED 1, WITHHELD 1, NOT_RECORDED 9.
A positive-control battery shows every intake code can fire, so zero rows in a tally mean untriggered rather than unreachable; it shows reachability only.
The defect battery establishes detection of the planted defects only, not the absence of every possible structural fault.
The author stresses the registry's finiteness: absences outside its eleven categories are not tracked, and extending it requires human judgment.
key_findings_evidence: Under this contract no input can make an absence look more settled than its most cautious observer reported.
The resulting state tally is NAMED 0, UNRESOLVED 1, WITHHELD 1, and NOT_RECORDED 9: eleven findings, one per record, as Proposition 5 requires.
Every member of the enumeration fires, so the zeros in the worked tally mean untriggered here.
the battery establishes detection of the planted defects, not the absence of every conceivable structural fault.
Eleven records name eleven categories a reviewer is prompted about; absences outside that list are not tracked, not flagged, and not counted as missing.
